outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to DeepSeekMath and the State of Mathematical Reasoning
outline.description: This chapter introduces the core problem of mathematical reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs), reviews the landscape of open vs. closed models, and presents the DeepSeekMath solution. It outlines the contributions of the paper, including scalable pre-training and novel Reinforcement Learning methodologies.
subtopics: The Challenge of Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
Limitations of Current Open-Source Models
Overview of DeepSeekMath Architecture and Capabilities
Key Contributions: Data Selection and GRPO
Benchmark Summary: Performance on MATH, GSM8K, and Multilingual Tasks

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Constructing the DeepSeekMath Corpus via Scalable Data Mining
outline.description: This chapter details the engineering behind creating a massive, high-quality mathematical dataset. It explains the methodology for extracting data from Common Crawl, ensuring quality through iterative filtering, handling data contamination (decontamination), and validating corpus efficacy.
subtopics: The DeepSeekMath Corpus Pipeline: From Common Crawl to 120B Tokens
FastText-Based Classification for Initial Filtering
Iterative Refinement Strategy: Expanding Seed Corpora and Domain Identification
Decontamination Techniques: Protecting Against Benchmark Leakage (GSM8K, MATH)
Validation Study: Comparing Against MathPile, OpenWebMath, and Proof-Pile-2
Analysis of Multilingual Impact (English vs. Chinese)

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Base Model Pre-Training and Instruction Tuning Strategies
outline.description: This chapter covers the supervised training phases that prepare DeepSeekMath before Reinforcement Learning begins. It discusses initialization choices (Coder vs. General LLMs), data composition ratios, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting strategies, and evaluation results on tool-use scenarios.
subtopics: [Initialization] Why Start with DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5?
[Composition] Balancing Math Tokens with Code and Natural Language Data
[Curriculum] Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with CoT, Program-of-Thought (PoT), and Tool Integration
[Tool Use] Program-Aided Reasoning with Python Libraries (Sympy/Math)
[Evaluation] Formal Theorem Proving on miniF2F Benchmark
[Baselines] Comparison against Mistral-7B, Llemma-34B, and Minerva-540B

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: Advanced Reinforcement Learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
outline.description: This technical chapter serves as a deep dive into GRPO. It contrasts GRPO with traditional Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), deriving the objective functions that eliminate the need for a separate value network/critic model while maintaining stability.
subtopics: [Comparison] PPO vs. GRPO: The Role of Value Functions in LLM Contexts
[Derivation] The GRPO Objective Function and Relative Advantage Estimation ($A_t$)
[Implementation Details]: Hyperparameters ($G$, Batch Size, KL Penalty Coefficient)
[Sampling Strategy] Generating Groups of Outputs from Single Questions

outline.chapter_title: : Supervising Policies with Process Rewards versus Outcome Rewards
outline.description: This section explores how rewards are applied during RL training. It distinguishes between evaluating only final answers (outcome) versus rewarding intermediate reasoning steps (process) to guide better mathematical derivations.
subtopics: [Conceptual Framework] Outcome Supervision RL ($r_{final}$)
[Refinement] Process Supervision RL ($r_{steps}$): Summing Normalized Rewards Across Steps
[Impact Analysis]: Why Process Supervision Improves Complex Reasoning Chains

outline.chapter_title: Understanding RL Dynamics Through a Unified Paradigm
outline.description: This chapter abstracts various training methods into a unified theoretical framework to explain *why* they work differently. It analyzes how Data Sources (online/offline), Algorithms, and Reward Functions interact to shape model gradients.
subtopics: Defining the Unified Paradigm: Gradient Components $(Data Source, Reward Funcn., Algorithm)$
Case Studies: SFT vs. RFT vs. DPO vs. PPO/GRPO
Comparative Analysis: Online Sampling Efficiency
Comparative Analysis: Gradient Magnitude Control via Reward Scaling
Experimental Findings on Iterative RL Updates

outline.chapter_title: Deep Dive into Pre-Training Experiments & Ablation Studies
outline.description: Beyond main results, this chapter investigates specific hypotheses tested during development to validate design decisions.
subtopics: Does Code Training Improve Mathematical Reasoning?
Evidence for Synergistic Effects Between Code and Math Tokens
Investigating ArXiv Papers as Pre-training Data: Effectiveness or Noise?
Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting in Mixed Token Training

outline.chapter_title: Post-Hoc Analysis: Interpreting Success Factors in DeepSeekMath RL
outline.description: An analytical breakdown of experimental results to understand fundamental mechanisms driving performance gains.
subtopics: Distribution Robustness vs Fundamental Capability Enhancement(Maj@K vs Pass@K)
Alignment Problems in Early SFT Models
The Misalignment Hypothesis in Mathematical Reasoning

outline.description: A concluding overview summarizing current achievements while honestly addressing gaps.
subtopics: Current Strengths vs Closed-Model Gaps(Geometry/Theorem Proofs)
Limitations on Few-Shot Generalization Compared to GPT-4
Engineering Challenges in Further Improving Data Pipelines
Future Pathways in Reward Modeling and Sampling Strategies
